extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks to evaluate the mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples spanning five primary tasks (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook question answering, and visual question answering), seven mathematical reasoning types, and diverse visual context types, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, and Jianfeng Gao. MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. In International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA collects 6,141 examples from 31 sources. 2,666 examples are gathered from 9 existing multimodal MathQA datasets (limited to up to 400 examples each). 2,739 examples are sourced from 19 existing VQA datasets selected through heuristic filtering of quantity words followed by manual majority-vote verification by three expert annotators (capped at 400 examples per dataset). 736 examples are newly created across three datasets: IQTest (228 examples from online learning puzzle test figures), FunctionQA (400 examples from functional plots), and PaperQA (107 examples from academic papers released in August 2023 on Hugging Face).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA, ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS), puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic paper figures released in August 2023 on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Candidate instances from over 70 VQA datasets were automatically filtered using a predefined dictionary of quantity words and numeric answers, yielding 4,949 candidate instances that underwent manual validation. To ensure balanced representation, each source dataset was capped at up to 400 examples. The final compiled benchmark of 6,141 examples was split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) using stratified random sampling with a minimum threshold of 4 questions per source dataset, maintaining total variation distance of 0.035 and KL divergence of 0.008.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Candidate VQA problems were labeled by three expert annotators using custom web annotation GUIs with majority voting to decide whether they involved mathematical reasoning. For the three new datasets, graduate students in STEM fields annotated problems, followed by a two-step process where three reviewers independently annotated each item and resolved discrepancies through group consensus discussion. For metadata verification, expert annotators manually annotated mathematical reasoning types on a sample of 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for identifying mathematical reasoning in candidate VQA problems was evaluated using Fleiss' Kappa, yielding 0.775. For the newly collected datasets, independent review across three reviewers showed an inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% (disagreements in 6 of 736 questions, resolved by consensus). For the 1,000-example metadata verification, 94.1% of examples shared the exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human labels, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; expert annotators
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is split into testmini (1,000 examples, publicly available) and test (5,141 examples, answer labels withheld to avoid data contamination). An online evaluation platform and leaderboard are maintained. The maintainers commit to updating the dataset to address potential data noise from community feedback and evolving the leaderboard with new foundation models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to facilitate the development of general-purpose AI assistants capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, such as solving problems in educational disciplines, aiding data analysts with logical queries over statistical data, and assisting in scientific discovery and theorem proving.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in representing certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. High-quality collection in specialized fields (e.g., college-level mathematics and science) is labor-intensive, impacting scalability and generalizability. Due to heterogeneous external sources, only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and annotations lack a unified format and structure.
